course_description:
In depth knowledge and practical skills required to understand how human activity and/or natural climatic variability has shaped the vegetated landscapes of the planet, particular links to fire and management.

An optional field trip will take place during the semester for an additional cost. Please see published course profile for further details.

Themes in the course will include: fire ecology; palaeoecology; the relative role people and natural climatic variability played in ecosystem change and the importance of fire in these alterations; and impacts of future environmental change on vegetated landscapes and fire management. Case studies will be used to illustrate these topics from a variety of Australian and international contexts. The course also includes themes covering the strategy, planning and on the ground execution of prescribed burning and controlling wildfire, with practical exercises to gain experience in the ecological and technical aspects related to fire ecology and palaeoecology.

An optional field trip will be held in week 5 which students may choose to attend. There will be an additional cost of approximately $20. Further details to be provided on Blackboard.

Students who are unable to attend this field trip will be provided with a desktop study to assist them with completing their assessments.

course_aims: This course aims to enable you to gain knowledge in the concepts and currentﾠissues in palaeoecology and fire ecology through an understanding of key processes, methods and techniques in these discliplines. A key link will be made to the importance of these topics in natural resource management and conservation. Case studies drawn from across the planet will be used to illustrate key concepts.

learning_outcomes.description: Take account of current debates in palaeoecology through understanding and reflection on the content of lectures, practicals and required readings.
Develop skills of research, analysis and argument in the areas of palaeoecology.
Describe key concepts in fire ecology, through understanding and reflection on the content of lectures, practicals and required readings.
Develop skills of research, analysis and argument in the areas of fire ecology.
Describe how key concepts in palaeoecology and fire ecology are crucial for effective natural resource management and conservation.
Describe how fire can impact Australian landscapes and key issues that need to be taken into account for planned burns.

assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
Practical assessment workbooks will be submitted at the end of each class for grading. The assessment is due at the end of the student's allocated practical session. If a student has an approved extension they will need to contact the course coordinator for instructions on how to submit.
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 28 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
If a student has an approved extension they will need to contact the course coordinator for instructions on how to submit.
Students that cannot attend a practical session under exceptional circumstances must complete an Absence Request Form (directions via Blackboard) and notify the course coordinator of an approval to receive alternative arrangements in order to be able to complete the practical submission. This is not an extension to the assessment due date. If a student does not attend a practical in order to complete their practical workbook and has not submitted an absence request form for approval, they will be unable to receive any marks for that particular workbook.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
You are required to submit assessable items on time. If you fail to meet the submission deadline for any assessment item, then 10% of the maximum possible mark for the assessment item (the assessment ‘marked from’ value) will be deducted as a late penalty for every day (or part day) late after the due date.
For example, if you submit your assignment 1 hour late, you will be penalised 10%; if your assignment is 24.5 hours late, you will be penalised 20% (because it is late by one 24-hour period plus part of another 24-hour period).

The report will be graded based on a criteria posted on Blackboard.
